A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Fast-ThinkAct paper, with complete main text, Appendices A–B, and references. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that all research content is identical; differences are confined to first-page date and version markings.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot-manipulation experiments, embodied-reasoning scores, latency measurements, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including Fast-ThinkAct benchmark results, latency measurements, and main-text and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical latent reasoning, preference-guided distillation, visual-plan alignment, policy learning, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin2.0, EgoPlan-Bench2, RoboVQA, OpenEQA, and RoboFAC, with the same few-shot and failure-analysis scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments. This includes DP, ACT, π0, RDT, and ThinkAct in Table 1, and the no-thinking, six-textual-token, and length-penalty alternatives in Table 6.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.4 retain the same metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation procedures, including 500 trials per LIBERO suite and 100 RoboTwin2.0 rollouts under each difficulty setting.

E4.justification: The loss and training-stage ablations, action-model conditioning analysis, latent-step sensitivity study, few-shot experiments, and qualitative failure analyses are identical in Section 4.3 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4.2 reports the same three random seeds for LIBERO. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 5 reports Fast-ThinkAct-3B scores of 89.7 on LIBERO and 68.7 on SimplerEnv-Google, with 805 ms latency, in both versions.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about verbalizable latent planning, up to 89.3% latency reduction, long-horizon planning, few-shot adaptation, and failure recovery.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Section 5 retains the same verbalizer-hallucination limitation and explanation of its relationship to action execution.

D1.justification: Implementation details in Section 4.1 and Appendix A, including hyperparameters, hardware, data processing, and verbalizer setup, are identical. The project-page link and supplementary-material references are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning statements, and all 76 reference entries are identical. No cited work or relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: The first-page header date changes from 2026-1-15 to 2026-2-25, and the arXiv stamp changes from v1, 14 Jan 2026 to v2, 24 Feb 2026. Body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10, Tables 1–8, Algorithm 1, captions, and their placement are unchanged. Pages 2–24 render identically, and first-page differences are limited to the date/version markings.

improvement.justification: v2 updates only the first-page date and version markings. The scientific content, empirical evidence, appendices, reproducibility information, and presentation remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
